egress.terms: Unmetered on an unlimited plan; article availability binds before bytes.

interface_detail: NNTP reader, TLS; standard article commands.
chaining: The clearest documented split between the two article codes: 423 means the group is there and the article is not, 430 means the article is unavailable while the group remains readable, which is what a script can branch on.

limits.value: articles past retention answer 423 or 430 per article id
plan connection count is the ceiling; excess connections are refused at connect time
50 SSL connections on the 12-month plan, 20 on the 1-month

limits_note: The vendor points at indexers as the amplifier: 'Many Indexers maintain references to articles long after they've been removed from Usenet servers', so the NZB can be valid and the articles still gone.
binding_note: Unlimited bytes; the first failure is a per-article 430/423 whose frequency is set by the indexer's freshness and the spool's retention.

identity_cost.detail: Paid account with email and card. No identity document described.

reliability_note: An indexer can point at articles the spool no longer holds; each such article is a per-file failure and only PAR2 or a second provider recovers it.
confidence_note: The 423/430 distinction and the indexer behaviour are the vendor's own. No removal-by-notice cause is named on this page, which differs from Newshosting's page in the same group.

evidence.proved: '423 No Such Article: The server acknowledges the group exists, but the article requested is not present. 430 No Such Article: The article is not available on the server, even though the newsgroup is accessible.' And 'Many Indexers maintain references to articles long after they've been removed from Usenet servers.'
Second server behaviour: a backup account is only asked after every primary has answered no such article; a second server turns a whole-release PAR2 read into one article fetch.

verdict.reason: The record's own free_tier says 'No free tier; a paid usenet account', and the plan is USD 7.95 on a 12-month term. 'qualifies' asserts a free path that does not exist; failure-modes recorded it by judging unlimited paid bandwidth as if it were free capacity.

binding.reason: Unlimited data and speed with 6,642 days of retention: at 1 TiB/month nothing in the vocabulary fails, and 50 connections is concurrency on a 12-month plan. retention-clamped describes a server shortening what was stored, not an article that has aged out of the spool.
